reference_scope: visible face/hair only; source age, identity, personality and body shape are not inferred
policy: strict partial_is_fail; any FAIL or UNOBSERVABLE blocks all-of PASS

gates.expected: Main subject visible face/hair qualitatively follows reference dark chin-length bob, separated wispy fringe, dark eyes and softly tapered jaw without transfer of reference outfit or crop.
gates.pass: All face and hair features are observable and reasonably corresponding.
gates.fail: Distinct incompatible visible face or hair construction.
gates.unobservable: Main face or hair obscured, blurred, too small or unavailable.
gates.image_grounded_evidence: Main woman has a dark jaw/chin-length bob, separated wispy fringe, dark eyes, tapered jaw and rounded lips corresponding qualitatively to the source face/hair. Work shirt, apron and workshop are new. This checks visible appearance, not identity.

gates.expected: Two newly designed adults in a theatrical costume repair room with a workbench and garment-rack context.
gates.pass: The central seamstress and performer are both visibly adult and the backstage repair setting reads as such.
gates.fail: Childlike subjects or materially different scene.
gates.unobservable: A subject age presentation or workshop context cannot be assessed.
gates.image_grounded_evidence: Two adult-presenting subjects stand beside an actual costume workbench with spools, garment racks, a dressed mannequin and task lights. Exact numerical ages are not measurable from pixels; newly authored adult scene is observable.

gates.expected: The seamstress right thumb and index pinch her own ivory apron top edge at upper chest, producing a local canvas fold.
gates.pass: Both digit-to-canvas contact and apron ownership are visible.
gates.fail: Hand floats, touches body instead, merely gestures near apron, or pinches other person garment.
gates.unobservable: Finger contact or apron ownership is occluded or cropped.
gates.image_grounded_evidence: At approximately x=500,y=585, the main right thumb and index grip the ivory apron upper edge and raise a small local canvas fold. The apron straps and bib continue on her own torso.

gates.expected: The seamstress right palm surface faces the lens at own-apron contact.
gates.pass: Palm skin and its inner surface are visible at that contact, with right limb continuity.
gates.fail: Dorsal hand surface faces camera or a different hand supplies the palm.
gates.unobservable: Palm surface or limb ownership cannot be traced.
gates.image_grounded_evidence: At the own-apron contact the visible surface is the back of her right hand, with knuckles and nails toward the lens. The palm creases specified in the frozen baseline are not camera-facing.

gates.expected: Seamstress left index curves beneath gold braid that remains attached to performer cape upper lapel.
gates.pass: A finger-under-cord contact and cord-to-performer-garment continuity are visible.
gates.fail: Finger points beside cord, grasps detached unrelated ornament, or touches own garment instead.
gates.unobservable: Cord contact or attachment cannot be resolved.
gates.image_grounded_evidence: At approximately x=1030,y=530 her left fingertips visibly hold a frayed gold knot/cord section attached to the performer cape. The specifically required left index curving beneath an attached braid is not separately readable; contact with the cord alone does not establish the hook mechanism.

gates.expected: Seamstress left hand back faces lens at performer cord contact, showing knuckles or nails.
gates.pass: Dorsal left surface and corresponding limb ownership are visible.
gates.fail: Palm faces lens or another owner supplies the dorsal hand.
gates.image_grounded_evidence: At the performer-cord contact the inner palm of her left hand faces the lens, including its palm surface; the dorsum with knuckles/nails facing the lens is absent. The connected left forearm confirms the owner.

gates.expected: Seamstress head modestly turns toward screen-right performer while eyes return toward the lens.
gates.pass: Both head turn and camera-directed pupil alignment are visible together.
gates.fail: Straight front head instead of modest turn, or gaze toward performer/down to task rather than camera.
gates.unobservable: Pupils or head orientation cannot be judged.
gates.image_grounded_evidence: Her head is modestly turned toward screen-right while both eyes return toward the lens. The face remains readable and her closed mouth forms a small asymmetric smile; the glance does not infer an emotional attitude.

gates.expected: Two short frayed cord ends hang below a small star brooch as immediate visible trace of cord snapping.
gates.pass: Brooch plus visibly separated/frayed braid ends coexist.
gates.fail: Continuous intact cord or missing visible snapped trace.
gates.unobservable: Ends/brooch too small, blurred or occluded.
gates.image_grounded_evidence: A frayed gold section is visible by the hand on the viewer-left lapel. The star brooch is on the opposite viewer-right side with a separate ornamental hanging cord/tassel. Two short frayed ends directly beneath the same star brooch are not established.

gates.expected: Frame includes both adult heads through upper hips and all main hand/wrist/forearm connections with both contact sites.
gates.pass: The specified crop and continuity preserve all consequential contacts.
gates.fail: Specified crop or clear limb connection is contradicted.
gates.unobservable: A consequential limb connection is hidden or a contact is outside frame.
gates.image_grounded_evidence: Both main wrist/forearm chains and both contact zones are visible in a landscape upper-hip frame, but the male performer crown is clipped by the top image boundary. The frozen gate requires both full adult heads through upper hips, so this partial match fails.

pixel_scope_note: The scene and its forms were independently authored before retrieval. Visible candidate-related forms are not proof that the integrated source caused the result; no before/after comparison is available.
